headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift the cost of grid infrastructure, including capacity and distribution, from residential users to large energy consumers like data centers, potentially saving residential customers money.
status: Last Action: Governor's Action Deadline 11:59 p.m., May 23, 2026 on 2026-04-22
supporters: Residential ratepayers, consumer advocacy groups, some lawmakers.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users, Dominion Energy (regarding amendments).
news_headline: Governor Amends Bills Shifting Costs to Data Centers
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger suggested changes to HB 1393, a key energy measure designed to shift more costs onto data centers to save residential electricity customers money and expand a power line burial program. Critics, including Dominion Energy, argue that the Governor's amendments undermine the bill's original goals of lowering costs for customers and reducing outages.

headline: Mandate Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water users providing water to data centers to report total monthly or quarterly water consumption, including reclaimed water, to the State Water Control Board for transparency.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, water conservationists, Potomac Conservancy, Sen. Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden).
news_headline: Data Centers Drinking Potomac Resources; Transparency Bill SB553
news_summary: The Potomac Conservancy is advocating for SB 553, a bill that requires data centers to report their water usage to the State Water Control Board, citing concerns about the Potomac River region's water supply failing to meet needs by 2030 due to data center consumption. This transparency is deemed critical for advocating for water-friendly infrastructure and combating data center sprawl.

headline: Regulate Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate site assessments for new high-energy use facilities, including noise studies and potential impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites, to mitigate negative effects on residential areas.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, Del. Joshua Thomas, Del. Sam Rasoul.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry (due to increased regulatory burden).
news_headline: Expert Weighs in on Virginia's New Data Center Laws
news_summary: University of Richmond professor Mary Finley-Brook discusses new Virginia laws regulating data centers, including measures addressing water usage, noise, and site suitability. She characterizes these as "moderate steps" towards regulation, noting that while some bills passed, comprehensive reform is still lacking, and debates continue over data center subsidies.
